AuditLogActionsFilter.description: Only return entries whose `action` is one of these names, matched exactly as recorded. Comma-separated.
AuditLogActionsFilter.name: actions

AuditLogActorIdsFilter.description: Only return entries performed by these users. Comma-separated user IDs. Available to organization accounts only; a personal or team account is answered 400.
AuditLogActorIdsFilter.name: actorIds

AuditLogEndTime.description: Latest instant to include, inclusive (RFC 3339). Must be after `startTime` when both are given; 400 otherwise.
AuditLogEndTime.name: endTime

AuditLogSearch.description: Case-insensitive substring match against `email`, `resourceType`, `resourceId`, `action` and `value`; `actorId` is not searched. Surrounding whitespace is ignored.
AuditLogSearch.name: search

AuditLogStartTime.description: Earliest instant to include, inclusive (RFC 3339). The account's audit log retention window still applies: entries that have aged out are not returned even when this reaches further back.
AuditLogStartTime.name: startTime

BillingBucketSize.description: Length of each billing time bucket. Defaults to day.
BillingBucketSize.name: bucketSize

BillingEndTime.description: End of the billing period (RFC 3339), exclusive. Defaults to now. Snapped up to the end of the bucketSize bucket it lands in (unless already on a boundary) so the window aligns with the returned records.
BillingEndTime.name: endTime

BillingLastN.description: Return the last N buckets of bucketSize, ending with the current (in-progress) bucket — e.g. lastN=100 with bucketSize=day is "last 100 days". The resolved window is aligned to bucket boundaries: startTime is the start of the earliest bucket (e.g. midnight of the earliest day) and endTime is the end of the current bucket. Mutually exclusive with startTime/endTime; provide one or the other, not both.
BillingLastN.name: lastN

BillingStartTime.description: Start of the billing period (RFC 3339). Defaults to 30 days ago. Snapped down to the start of its bucketSize bucket so the window aligns with the returned records; provide a boundary-aligned value (e.g. midnight for bucketSize=day) to avoid widening.
BillingStartTime.name: startTime

CatalogIncludeParam.description: Comma-separated optional expansions. Supported value today: AVAILABILITY. This may expand with more include values in the future.
CatalogIncludeParam.name: include

CountryCodesFilter.description: Comma-separated ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country codes, uppercase, to constrain availability to — e.g. FR or FR,DE. Values within this filter use OR semantics. Valid only with include=AVAILABILITY (400 otherwise); a malformed entry is a 422. Scopes availability, lowest-price calculations and the dataCenters array to those countries, so a listed data center outside them is omitted rather than returned with availability NONE. On the list endpoint a GPU type with no data center in those countries drops out entirely; the single-GPU endpoint still returns the requested type, with availability NONE and dataCenters omitted, so a 404 keeps meaning the GPU type does not exist. Read the NONE on availability rather than the absence of dataCenters, which is also absent when availability was not requested.
CountryCodesFilter.name: countryCodes

CpuProductFilter.description: Comma-separated availability product contexts. Supported values for CPUs: POD, SERVERLESS. Required with include=AVAILABILITY, and valid only with it (400 either way). There is no default: availability differs by product.
CpuProductFilter.name: product

CpuVCPUCountFilter.description: Availability vCPU count. Valid only with include=AVAILABILITY. Must be a power of two.
CpuVCPUCountFilter.name: vcpuCount

CudaVersionsFilter.description: Comma-separated CUDA versions to scope availability and lowest-price calculations to, matched exactly. Format: major.minor, e.g. 12.8 — a bare major is rejected here because it identifies no version. Valid only with include=AVAILABILITY (400 otherwise) and mutually exclusive with minCudaVersion (400 if both are sent); a malformed entry is a 422. Also narrows the returned cudaVersions array; omit it to enumerate every version offered.
CudaVersionsFilter.name: cudaVersions

GpuCloudFilter.description: Cloud type for availability and lowest-price calculations. Valid only with include=AVAILABILITY. Supported values: SECURE, COMMUNITY. Upstream default when omitted: SECURE.
GpuCloudFilter.name: cloud

GpuCountFilter.description: GPU count for availability and lowest-price calculations. Valid only with include=AVAILABILITY. Defaults to 1.
GpuCountFilter.name: count

GpuProductFilter.description: Comma-separated availability product contexts. Supported values: POD, CLUSTER, SERVERLESS. Required with include=AVAILABILITY, and valid only with it (400 either way). There is no default: the same GPU type can be scarce for pods and plentiful for serverless, so the context has to be stated rather than assumed.
GpuProductFilter.name: product

LogLastEventID.description:
SSE reconnect cursor — a timestamp emitted by this endpoint. Takes
precedence over `since` and `tail`: when present, the stream resumes
from this point. Sent automatically by EventSource on reconnect.
LogLastEventID.name: Last-Event-ID

LogSince.description:
RFC3339 timestamp to resume from. Ignored when `Last-Event-ID` is
provided. When set, the stream resumes from this point and `tail` is
ignored.
LogSince.name: since

LogSourceParam.description: Log source to stream. Omit to include both container and system logs.
LogSourceParam.name: source

LogTail.description:
Number of historical lines to backfill before streaming. Defaults to
100 when omitted; set `0` to stream live with no backfill. Maximum 5000.
Ignored when `since` or `Last-Event-ID` is provided — the resume cursor
drives the backfill instead.
LogTail.name: tail

MinCudaVersionFilter.description: Lowest acceptable CUDA version to scope availability and lowest-price calculations to, compared numerically. Format: integer major or major.minor, e.g. 12 or 12.1 — unlike the `gpu.minCudaVersion` body field on pod and endpoint create, a bare major is accepted here and means any release of that major, because this filter only widens a read. Valid only with include=AVAILABILITY (400 otherwise) and mutually exclusive with cudaVersions (400 if both are sent); a malformed value is a 422. Use this for an open-ended floor and cudaVersions for an exact set.
MinCudaVersionFilter.name: minCudaVersion

PaginationCursor.description: Opaque resume cursor — pass the previous response's `pagination.nextCursor` through verbatim; omit for the first page. A cursor is only valid for the operation and parameters that issued it; a malformed or foreign cursor is rejected with 422.
PaginationCursor.name: cursor

PaginationLimit.description: Page size, 1–1000. Defaults to 1000 when omitted.
PaginationLimit.name: limit

PaginationLimitAuditLogs.description: Page size, 1–200. Defaults to 200 when omitted.
PaginationLimitAuditLogs.name: limit

PaginationLimitBuilds.description: Page size, 1–100. Defaults to 100 when omitted.
PaginationLimitBuilds.name: limit

BadRequestError.description: The request could not be processed because it is malformed or conflicts with request rules.

ForbiddenError.description: The bearer token is valid, but it does not grant access to the requested resource or action.

value.detail: The requested method is not allowed for this path.
value.title: Method Not Allowed

MethodNotAllowedError.description: The request method is not supported for the target path.

Allow.description: Comma-separated methods supported by the target path.

NotFoundError.description: The requested resource was not found or is not accessible to the caller.

value.detail: Request body exceeds the 1048576 byte limit.
value.title: Request Entity Too Large

RequestTooLargeError.description:
The incoming request body exceeds 1048576 bytes (1 MiB). Body size is
checked after authentication and rate limiting. GET and DELETE reject
any nonempty request body with `422` instead.

An operation can also return this status when its expanded upstream
request is too large, even if the incoming body is within the limit.

value.detail: Response too large for one request. Request fewer items and retry.
value.title: Request Entity Too Large

ResponseTooLargeError.description:
The response would exceed the upstream response size cap. Request
fewer items and retry; on paginated operations, lower `limit`.

value.detail: rate limit exceeded for the minute window
value.title: Too Many Requests

TooManyRequestsError.description: The caller exceeded its per-user rate limit. The response identifies the window that was exceeded and how long to wait. The `RateLimit` and `RateLimit-Policy` headers (per the IETF ratelimit-headers draft) also accompany successful responses, so clients can track quota before a 429.

Retry-After.description: Seconds to wait before retrying, per the exceeded window.

UnauthorizedError.description: Authentication failed because the bearer token is missing, malformed, expired, or invalid.

UnprocessableEntityError.description: The request body or parameters were syntactically valid but failed validation.

AuditLog.description: One recorded action on the account.

action.description: Name of the action, as recorded at write time. Not an enum: values are free-form, mostly lower case verbs, and new actions appear without an API version change. Current writers record values such as `create`, `update`, `delete`, `rename`, `lock`, `unlock`, `start`, `reset`, `add` and `setBillingMode`.

actorId.description: ID of the user who performed the action. Null when the action was not attributable to a user.

email.description: Email of the actor when the action was recorded. Null when unknown.

resourceId.description: ID of the affected resource. Empty when the action was not about one resource; a bulk action lists every affected ID, comma-separated.

resourceType.description: Kind of resource the action applied to, as recorded at write time. Not an enum: values are free-form, mostly lower camel case, and new kinds appear without an API version change. Current writers record values such as `pod`, `apiKey`, `sharedApiKey`, `secret`, `costCenter`, `paymentMethod`, `billingAccount`, `registryCredential`, `organization` and `group`, and `unknown` when the writer recorded no kind.

timestamp.description: When the action happened (UTC, whole seconds).

value.description: Details of the change as a JSON-encoded string. The structure varies by action; parse it as JSON for a structured view. A bulk action split across several entries adds an `auditChunk` object with `index` and `of`. Null when the action recorded no details.

BaseContainerConfig.description: Container configuration universal to every containerized resource. Compose ContainerConfig instead unless the resource cannot support a direct registry credential (clusters — there the registry credential arrives via a pod template, see CreateClusterRequest.templateId).

args.description:
The container's command, as a single raw string. This is the field `entrypoint` and `cmd` encode into, exposed in its stored form.

Two shapes are accepted. A bare shell string is treated as CMD and split into arguments, which is what the console's "Container start command" field writes. A JSON object of the form `{"entrypoint":[...],"cmd":[...]}` sets either or both explicitly.

Responses always return both representations: `args` exactly as stored, plus the deconstructed `entrypoint` and `cmd`. Supplying `args` together with `entrypoint` or `cmd` is allowed only when they describe the same command, so a read-modify-write client can send back everything it received. Send `""` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.

cmd.description: Container CMD in exec form. When the image defines an ENTRYPOINT, this is the argument list passed to it. Encoded into the `args` field; supplying both is allowed only when they describe the same command. Send `[]` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.

disk.description: Container disk in GB (ephemeral, wiped on restart)

entrypoint.description: Container ENTRYPOINT in exec form, overriding the image's own. Encoded into `args` field; supplying both is allowed only when they describe the same command. Send `[]` to clear, omit to leave unchanged.

id.description: CPU flavor identifier, as returned by GET /v2/catalog/cpus.

vcpuCount.description: Number of vCPUs. Must be valid for the selected CPU flavor and must be a power of two.

excludedTypes.description:
GPU **type** IDs to subtract from the selected pools — the `id`
field of `GET /v2/catalog/gpus`, the same identifiers pods take in
`gpu.id`. Workers run on every type in `pools` except these. Omit to
use the whole pool.

Pools stay the unit of selection; types are the unit of
subtraction. There is no inclusive allowlist: a card later added to
one of your pools becomes eligible, which is the honest reading of
"this pool, minus these".

Tied to `pools`, because the two together are one selection:
supplying `pools` replaces that selection wholesale, so a `PATCH`
sending `pools` **without `excludedTypes`** **clears** them —
restate them to keep them. A `PATCH` that omits `pools` leaves both
the pools and the exclusions untouched, so changing only a CUDA
constraint cannot widen a pinned endpoint.

Rejected with 400 if a value is not a GPU type in one of `pools`;
upstream accepts unrecognized exclusions silently, so a typo would
otherwise produce a filter that does nothing. Surrounding whitespace
is trimmed, so `" NVIDIA L40"` and `"NVIDIA L40"` mean the same card.

pools.description:
Serverless GPU pool IDs (as returned by `GET /v2/catalog/gpus` in
`pool`). Workers are placed on whichever listed pool has capacity.
Narrow a pool down to specific cards with `excludedTypes`.

On `PATCH`, `pools` and `excludedTypes` are one selection and are
replaced together, so sending `pools` by itself **clears the
exclusions**. Two cases:

- **Changing pools, keeping exclusions** — send both fields in one
  request: `{"gpu": {"pools": ["ADA_24"], "excludedTypes":
  ["NVIDIA L40"]}}`. `GET` the endpoint first to read the current
  `excludedTypes` and resend the ones that still apply to the new
  pools; an exclusion naming a type outside `pools` is a 400.
- **Changing only `count` or a CUDA constraint** — omit `pools`:
  `{"gpu": {"minCudaVersion": "12.4"}}`. The pool list and the
  exclusions are both left exactly as they are.

`excludedTypes` documents the full rule.

BaseMounts.description:
The mount kinds every resource that takes `mounts` shares. At-most-one
of `persistent` or `network` may be set today (mutually exclusive,
enforced at the handler with 400 if both are present). The `network`
field is an array for forward compatibility with eventual
multi-network-volume support, but `maxItems` is 1 today. Left open so
that concrete schemas can extend it and close themselves.

BillingAmounts.description: Total spend across all billable Runpod resources with each cost component broken out, fully prefixed by resource. Backs the aggregate record's amounts and the metadata totals. Serverless amounts are inclusive of platform charges.

clusterDiskAmount.description: Cluster disk cost in USD for the bucket.

clusterGpuAmount.description: Cluster GPU compute cost in USD for the bucket.

clusterNetworkingAmount.description: Cluster inter-node networking cost in USD for the bucket.

endpointAmount.description: Runpod public endpoint cost in USD for the bucket.

podCpuAmount.description: CPU pod compute cost in USD for the bucket.

podDiskAmount.description: Pod disk cost in USD for the bucket.

podGpuAmount.description: GPU pod compute cost in USD for the bucket.

serverlessCpuAmount.description: Serverless CPU compute cost in USD for the bucket.

serverlessDiskAmount.description: Serverless disk cost in USD for the bucket.

serverlessFeeAmount.description: Unused and always 0. Platform charges are included in the serverless compute amounts.

serverlessGpuAmount.description: Serverless GPU compute cost in USD for the bucket.

storageHighPerformanceAmount.description: High-performance network volume storage cost in USD for the bucket.

storageStandardAmount.description: Standard network volume storage cost in USD for the bucket.

totalAmount.description: Total cost in USD for the bucket across all resources.

BillingBucketSize.description: Length of each billing time bucket.

BillingQuery.description: Resolved query window and granularity (routes without a filter).

BillingRecord.description: A single time-bucketed record of total spend across all billable Runpod resources, with each cost component broken out. Returned by GET /v2/billing.

BillingTimeRange.description: Half-open time range [startTime, endTime) in RFC 3339. On a record it is the time bucket; on a query echo it is the resolved window.

branch.description: Git branch the commit was pushed to.

commitDate.description: When the triggering commit was authored.

commitHash.description: Short hash of the commit that triggered the build.

completedAt.description: When the build reached a terminal state. Null while the build is live.

error.description: Failure detail for `FAILED` / `TEST_FAILED` builds; null otherwise.

imageName.description: Fully qualified image the build produced (or will produce).

startedAt.description: When the build started. Null while the build is still pending.

BuildState.description:
GitHub build lifecycle state. `COMPLETED`, `FAILED`, `CANCELLED`, and
`TEST_FAILED` are terminal; `PENDING`, `BUILDING`, `UPLOADING`, and
`TESTING` are live.

CatalogInclude.description: Catalog include expansion. Only AVAILABILITY is supported today; additional include values may be added in the future.

Cloud.description:
Cloud tier.
- `SECURE`    — Runpod-owned datacenter hardware
- `COMMUNITY` — community-hosted hardware

Cluster.description: A cluster. Cluster-level fields describe the identity and homogeneous shape; `pods` is a lightweight summary of the members. Fetch the full member pods — with their container config, mounts, and runtime state — from `GET /v2/clusters/{id}/pods`.

dataCenterId.description: Data center the cluster is placed in (a cluster is always within a single data center). Derived from the member pods; omitted until at least one pod is placed.

network.description: The cluster's overlay network; omitted until the network is provisioned.

primary.description: The primary (master) node; omitted until a primary pod is placed. Its `sshEndpoint` is omitted until that pod is RUNNING with SSH exposed.

template.description: ID of the template this cluster's pods were created from; omitted when they were not created from one.

ClusterBillingAmounts.description: Cluster cost components (GPU-only, no CPU). Backs a record's amounts and the metadata totals.

diskAmount.description: Cluster disk cost in USD for the bucket.

gpuAmount.description: Cluster GPU compute cost in USD for the bucket.

networkingAmount.description: Cluster inter-node networking cost in USD for the bucket.

totalAmount.description: Total Instant Cluster cost in USD for the bucket.

recordCount.description: Number of records returned (buckets times distinct clusters).

uniqueClusterCount.description: Number of distinct clusters the records span.

clusterId.description: The clusterId filter applied, if any.
The cluster this record bills. When the clusterId filter is set every record carries that id; otherwise one record is emitted per cluster per bucket.

ClusterBillingRecord.description: A single time-bucketed cluster billing record; clusters are GPU-only (no CPU component). Returned by GET /v2/billing/clusters.

ClusterCompute.description: The homogeneous compute shape of a cluster. Every pod in the cluster is identical: `podCount` pods, each with `gpuCountPerPod` GPUs of type `gpuTypeId`. Total GPUs = `podCount` * `gpuCountPerPod`.

gpuCountPerPod.description: Number of GPUs on each pod. Bounded above by the GPU type's per-cloud maximum (GpuType.maxCount); the upstream rejects values beyond it.

gpuTypeId.description: GPU type for every pod in the cluster, as returned by GET /v2/catalog/gpus.

podCount.description: Number of pods (nodes) in the cluster.

ClusterMounts.description:
Storage mounts for a cluster create: `persistent` or `network`, not
both. Clusters cannot mount global volumes, so `global` is rejected
with 422. A mount `path` must not be empty (rejected with 422):
upstream reads an empty path as unset and would mount the volume at
the template's path, or `/workspace` without a template.

ClusterNetwork.description: The cluster's private VXLAN overlay network (shared by all member pods).

vxlanId.description: VXLAN network identifier; omitted until assigned.

vxlanPort.description: UDP port carrying the VXLAN traffic; omitted until assigned.

ClusterPodsSummary.description: A lightweight summary of a cluster's member pods. Use `GET /v2/clusters/{id}/pods` to retrieve the full pod objects.

byStatus.description: Member pod counts keyed by pod status (the same values as `Pod.status`, e.g. RUNNING, PROVISIONING). Statuses with no pods are omitted.

total.description: Number of member pods currently provisioned for the cluster.

ClusterPrimary.description: The cluster's primary (master) node, through which the cluster is typically driven. Omitted until a primary pod has been placed.

podId.description: ID of the primary member pod.

sshEndpoint.description: Public SSH endpoint (`host:port`) for the primary node; omitted when the primary is not yet RUNNING or does not expose SSH (22/tcp).

ClusterType.description: Cluster type. TRAINING is the generic distributed-training cluster; SLURM provisions a managed Slurm controller/compute topology; RAY provisions a managed Ray head/worker topology; APPLICATION is a general multi-node application cluster.

registry.description: Container registry credential ID (for private images)

ContainerConfig.description: Reusable container configuration shared across templates, pods, and serverless endpoints. Adding a field here automatically propagates to all three resources.

memory.description: Memory allocated to the pod in GB.

CpuProduct.description: CPU catalog product availability context. Availability is product-specific, so this is required whenever availability is requested.

availability.description: Overall CPU availability for the requested `product` contexts. Present only when requested with include=AVAILABILITY, which also requires `product`.

dataCenters.description:
Per-datacenter CPU availability for the requested `product`
contexts, listing only the datacenters that offer this CPU flavor.
Present only when requested with include=AVAILABILITY, which also
requires `product`, and omitted entirely when the flavor is
unavailable everywhere.

id.description: CPU flavor identifier (use in cpu.id for pod creation)

securePerVcpu.description:
Price for secure pods per vCPU. Multiply by the chosen vCPU
count (within `vcpu.min`..`vcpu.max`) to get the total price.

serverlessPerVcpu.description:
Price for serverless per vCPU. Multiply by the chosen vCPU
count (within `vcpu.min`..`vcpu.max`) to get the total price.

ramGbPerVcpu.description:
GB of RAM allocated per vCPU. Multiply by the chosen vCPU
count (within `vcpu.min`..`vcpu.max`) to get the total RAM
for an instance of this flavor. May be fractional.

allOf.description:
Request body for creating a cluster. `compute` defines the
homogeneous pod shape; the container configuration (image, env, ports,
…) applies to every pod. Pass `templateId` to provision every member
pod from a pod template instead of inline container fields — the
template also supplies the container registry credential, the only
private-image path for clusters (a bare `registry` property on this
body is rejected).

dataCenterIds.description:
Preferred data centers for placement. Omit or pass an empty
array to let the scheduler choose. A cluster is always placed
within a single data center.

startJupyter.description: Start Jupyter on every member pod, as on pod create.

startSsh.description: Provision SSH access on every member pod: injects a PUBLIC_KEY environment variable carrying your account's registered SSH public key. Same semantics as the pod create flag.

templateId.description:
ID of a pod template to provision every member pod from. The
template supplies the container settings (image, args, disk,
env, ports) and the container registry credential for private
images — the only private-image path for clusters. Mutually
exclusive with `image`, `args`, `entrypoint`, `cmd`, `disk`,
`env`, and `ports` (rejected with 400). `mounts` combines with
it: the volume in `mounts` is attached to every member pod,
overriding the template's volume settings. The cluster
retains the link: the `template` response field is set. Must be
a non-serverless pod template accessible to the caller.

allowedCudaVersions.description:
Acceptable CUDA versions for worker placement, as
`major.minor`. Omit to accept any version (or inherit the
template's constraint when creating from `templateId`).
Matching is exact — discover valid values per GPU type via
`GET /v2/catalog/gpus?include=AVAILABILITY&product=SERVERLESS`
(`cudaVersions`).

A non-empty set is mutually exclusive with minCudaVersion (400
if both are sent). An explicit `[]` states no constraint, so it
may accompany a floor.

minCudaVersion.description:
Lowest acceptable CUDA version for worker placement, as
`major.minor`, compared numerically rather than as a decimal —
so 12.11 is above 12.2. Use this for an open-ended floor and
allowedCudaVersions for an exact set.

Mutually exclusive with a non-empty allowedCudaVersions (400 if
both are sent); an explicit `[]` there states no constraint and
may accompany this floor.

CreateEndpointGpuConfig.description:
GPU request for an endpoint create. Carries the CUDA constraints, which
live here rather than at the body's top level so they are
unrepresentable on a CPU endpoint.

cpu.description:
Eligible CPU configurations for each worker. Memory is derived from the
selected flavor's catalog RAM multiplier. Exact duplicate configurations
are rejected; the same flavor may be listed at different vCPU counts.

dataCenterIds.description: Preferred data centers for placement. Omit or pass an empty array to let the scheduler choose.

templateId.description:
ID of a serverless template to base this endpoint on. The
template is resolved at create time into the same container
settings you could otherwise spread into this body (image,
args, disk, ports, env, registry); explicit body fields
override the template's, except `env`, which is merged per
key with body values winning. The template's
allowedCudaVersions seeds `gpu.allowedCudaVersions` when the
body omits it — but only for a GPU create, since a CPU endpoint
has no gpu block to seed into, and not when the body sets
`gpu.minCudaVersion`, since seeding a set beside a floor would
manufacture the mutual-exclusion 400 from a valid request. Its
pod-specific startSsh/startJupyter flags are
ignored. Later template edits do not affect the endpoint.
The template may be one of your own or a public catalog
template — see `GET /v2/catalog/templates` (unknown or
inaccessible ID → 404) — and must be a serverless template
(→ 422).

type.description:
Request-routing model. Required — it determines the valid scaler
and request URLs, so it must be chosen explicitly on every create.

name.description: Human-readable name, 1–191 characters with at least one non-whitespace character. Leading and trailing whitespace is trimmed.

allowedCudaVersions.description:
Acceptable CUDA versions for the host machine, as `major.minor`.
Omit to accept any version. Matching is exact, so a version no
machine reports yields a capacity error rather than a fallback —
discover valid values per GPU type via
`GET /v2/catalog/gpus?include=AVAILABILITY&product=POD`
(`cudaVersions`).

A non-empty set is mutually exclusive with minCudaVersion (400
if both are sent). An explicit `[]` states no constraint, so it
may accompany a floor.

minCudaVersion.description:
Lowest acceptable CUDA version for the host machine, as
`major.minor`, compared numerically rather than as a decimal —
so 12.11 is above 12.2. Use this for an open-ended floor and
allowedCudaVersions for an exact set.

Mutually exclusive with a non-empty allowedCudaVersions (400 if
both are sent); an explicit `[]` there states no constraint and
may accompany this floor.

minRamPerGpu.description: Minimum host system RAM in GB per requested GPU. This is a placement filter, not a resource request. The actual total allocated system RAM may be higher and is returned in gpu.memory.

minVcpuCountPerGpu.description: Minimum host vCPU count per requested GPU. This is a placement filter, not a resource request. The actual total allocated vCPU count may be higher and is returned in gpu.vcpuCount.

CreateGpuConfig.description:
GPU request for a pod create. Carries the CUDA host constraints, which
live here rather than at the body's top level so they are
unrepresentable on a CPU pod.

dataCenter.description: Data center in which to create the volume

type.description:
Storage tier for the volume. Optional. When omitted, the volume is
provisioned using the requested data center's default (primary)
storage tier. HIGH_PERFORMANCE provisions a high-performance (HPS)
volume; STANDARD provisions a standard volume. A volume's tier is
immutable after creation.

allOf.description:
Request body for creating a pod. Exactly one of `gpu` or `cpu`
must be set — enforced at the handler layer. For CPU pods, memory
is derived by the API from the selected flavor's RAM multiplier;
clients provide only CPU flavor and vCPU count. CPU pods support
container disk, network volumes, and a global volume;
`mounts.persistent` is invalid when `cpu` is set.

`image` is required unless `templateId` is set.

cloud.description: Cloud tier. Defaults to `SECURE` when omitted.

dataCenterIds.description:
Preferred data centers for placement. Omit or pass an empty
array to let the scheduler choose.

globalNetworking.description: Enable global networking, giving the pod a private IP reachable across data centers. Requires an NVIDIA GPU and a global-networking-enabled data center (both enforced upstream). See `GET /v2/catalog/datacenters` (`globalNetwork`) for eligible data centers.

startJupyter.description:
Create-time flag telling the provisioner to start JupyterLab:
injects a generated `JUPYTER_PASSWORD` environment variable,
unless the request already sets one. Only images that honor
the convention start Jupyter from it (Runpod official images
do); expose `8888/http` in `ports` to reach it.

Not part of the pod's readable config — never returned by
GET and not changeable by PATCH.

startSsh.description:
Create-time flag telling the provisioner to set up SSH
access: injects a `PUBLIC_KEY` environment variable carrying
your account's registered SSH public keys, unless the request
already sets one. **Requires registered keys** (`PUT
/v2/account/ssh-keys`) — with none registered the flag does
nothing and the pod has no SSH access. Only images that honor
the convention start sshd from it (all Runpod official images
do). Connect using the pod's `ssh` block; the `ssh.direct`
variant additionally needs a `22/tcp` entry in `ports`.

Not part of the pod's readable config — never returned by
GET and not changeable by PATCH.

templateId.description:
ID of a pod template to base this pod on. The template is
resolved at create time into the same container settings you
could otherwise spread into this body (image, args, disk,
ports, env, registry, persistent mount, startSsh,
startJupyter, allowedCudaVersions); explicit body fields
override the template's, except `env`, which is merged per
key with body values winning. Sending either CUDA field
(`gpu.allowedCudaVersions` or `gpu.minCudaVersion`) replaces
the template's CUDA constraint entirely, and CPU pods ignore
it (like the persistent mount). The template is a one-time
source of settings: later template edits do not affect the
pod, and the created pod does not retain a link to the
template (`template` stays null). The template may be one
of your own or a public catalog template — see
`GET /v2/catalog/templates` (unknown or inaccessible ID →
404) — and must not be a serverless template (→ 422). CPU
pods do not inherit a template's persistent mount.

password.description: Registry password (write-only, not returned in responses)

username.description: Registry username (write-only, not returned in responses)

description.description: Optional human-readable description, at most 65,535 bytes of UTF-8 text.

name.description: Unique name for the secret — referenced from environment variables as `{{ RUNPOD_SECRET_<name> }}`; immutable after creation. Maximum 191 characters, must start with a letter or underscore, and may contain letters, digits, and `_.-/`. Names beginning with the reserved prefix `RUNPOD` are rejected (case-insensitive).

value.description: The secret value. Write-only — never returned by the API. Must be smaller than 16 MiB of UTF-8 text (strictly under 16,777,216 bytes).

allowedCudaVersions.description:
Acceptable CUDA versions for containers created from this
template, as `major.minor`. Omit to accept any version — see
the same field on `createPod` for matching semantics.
Expanded into GPU pod and serverless endpoint creates; CPU
pods ignore it.

startJupyter.description:
Start JupyterLab in containers created from this template:
injects a generated `JUPYTER_PASSWORD` environment variable,
unless `env` already sets one. Only images that honor the
convention start Jupyter from it (Runpod official images do);
expose `8888/http` in `ports` to reach it. Defaults to `true`
when omitted, matching console-created templates.

startSsh.description:
Provision SSH access in containers created from this template:
injects a `PUBLIC_KEY` environment variable carrying the
deployer's registered SSH public keys (`PUT
/v2/account/ssh-keys` — with none registered the flag does
nothing), unless `env` already sets one. Only images that
honor the convention start sshd from it (all Runpod official
images do); direct SSH also needs a `22/tcp` entry in
`ports`. Defaults to `true` when omitted, matching
console-created templates.

available.description: True when at least one machine on this CUDA version has free capacity now. False means the version is offered for this GPU type but is currently full, so a pod constrained to it will fail on capacity.

version.description: CUDA version as `major.minor`, suitable for `gpu.allowedCudaVersions` on pod create.

compliance.description: Compliance certifications held by this data center

cpuAvailability.description:
Availability of each CPU flavor this data center offers. Present
only when requested with include=CPU_AVAILABILITY, and omitted
entirely when the data center offers no CPU flavors.

globalNetwork.description: Whether this data center supports global networking (private cross-datacenter pod-to-pod network).

gpuAvailability.description:
Availability of each GPU this data center offers. Present only when
requested with include=GPU_AVAILABILITY, and omitted entirely when
the data center offers no GPUs.

networkVolumeTypes.description: Network volume tiers this DC supports. Empty = none.

DataCenterRegion.description: Continental region containing the data center.

delegatorUserId.description: User ID that created the delegation

dockerRegistryUri.description: Formatted ECR registry URI for Docker login

cpu.description:
Eligible CPU configurations for each worker, in the order they
were submitted. Present for CPU endpoints and omitted for GPU
endpoints. Memory is derived from the selected flavor's catalog
RAM multiplier.

EndpointBillingAmounts.description: Runpod public endpoint cost. Backs a record's amounts and the metadata totals.

totalAmount.description: Total public endpoint cost in USD for the bucket.

EndpointBillingRecord.description: A single time-bucketed Runpod public endpoint billing record. Returned by GET /v2/billing/endpoints.

allowedCudaVersions.description: Acceptable CUDA versions for worker placement, as `major.minor`. Empty means any version.

minCudaVersion.description: Lowest acceptable CUDA version for worker placement, as `major.minor`. Null means no floor.

EndpointMount.description:
A volume mounted on every worker, always at `/runpod-volume`. Custom
paths are not supported yet.

volumeId.description: ID of a NetworkVolume (under `network`) or GlobalVolume (under `global`).

EndpointMounts.description: Volumes mounted on every worker of the endpoint.

EndpointMountsInput.description:
Volumes to mount on the endpoint's workers. A `network` or `global`
list that is present replaces the endpoint's current list of that kind;
an empty list detaches it, and an omitted list is left unchanged. Both
kinds cannot be present on the endpoint at once, so to switch kinds send
`[]` for one and the new list for the other in the same request. Changes
apply to workers created afterwards. At most one global volume, GPU
endpoints only. `network` may accompany the deprecated `networkVolumes` field
only if the two agree exactly.

network.description: Network volumes, at most one per data center.

EndpointRequestUrls.description:
Request URLs appropriate to the endpoint's top-level `type`.
Queue-based endpoints provide job submission and management URLs;
load-balancing endpoints provide `base` and `health` because their
remaining paths are worker-defined.

Request and response bodies for the queue-based URLs are documented in
the [serverless operation reference](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/operation-reference).
Load-balancing endpoints are documented in
[Load balancing endpoints](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/load-balancing/overview).

EndpointScaling.description:
Autoscaling signal — a discriminated union on `type`: `QUEUE_DELAY`
(queue-based endpoints only) or `REQUEST_COUNT`. The scaler is chosen
independently of the endpoint's routing `type` and can be switched on
update.

EndpointType.description:
Request-routing semantics for a modern serverless endpoint.
- `QUEUE` — submit asynchronous or synchronous jobs through the managed queue.
- `LOAD_BALANCER` — send requests directly to worker-defined HTTP paths.
  Configure via `env`: `PORT` (server port, default 80), `PORT_HEALTH`
  (health-check port, default 80), and `HEALTH_CHECK_PATH` (path the
  load balancer polls for worker health, default `/ping`).

idleTimeout.description:
Seconds before idle workers scale down. Not applicable to queue-based
endpoints scaling on `requestCount` — rejected on create/update and
omitted from responses for that combination.

FlashBoot.description:
FlashBoot cold-start acceleration mode.
- `OFF`                — disabled
- `FLASHBOOT`          — enabled
- `PRIORITY_FLASHBOOT` — enabled with priority capacity

GlobalMount.description:
Reference to a GlobalVolume. Usage-billed, so it has no size. The
underlying `volumeId` is immutable post-create; the mount `path` may be
changed via PATCH.

path.description: Mount path inside the container. Optional on create, where a default is chosen for you; a PATCH that omits it leaves the path unchanged.

createdByUserId.description: ID of the user who created the volume, if known

name.description: Human-readable name (not required to be unique)

memory.description: Total system RAM in GB allocated to the pod across all requested GPUs.

vcpuCount.description: Total vCPU count allocated to the pod across all requested GPUs.

availability.description: Overall GPU availability for the requested `product` contexts. Present only when requested with include=AVAILABILITY, which also requires `product`.

cudaVersions.description:
CUDA versions offered by machines with this GPU type, each tagged
with current capacity. Present only when requested with
include=AVAILABILITY, and scoped by the same filters as
`availability` (`count`, `cloud`, `product`, and whichever of
`cudaVersions` / `minCudaVersion` was supplied).

Machines that report no CUDA version are skipped, so this property
is absent entirely for a GPU type with none — AMD, for instance.
Treat a missing `cudaVersions` the same as an empty one. A version
absent from a populated list is not offered for this GPU type.

dataCenters.description:
Per-datacenter GPU availability for the requested `product`
contexts, listing only the datacenters that offer this GPU in the
requested configuration. Present only when requested with
include=AVAILABILITY, which also requires `product`, and omitted
entirely when the configuration is unavailable everywhere.

id.description: Individual GPU type identifier (use for pod creation)

maxCount.description:
The largest number of GPUs you can request on a single pod of this
type, quoted separately per cloud. A pod runs on one machine, so
this is the GPU count of the largest machine of this type Runpod
operates in that cloud.

This is a ceiling, not a stock level — it does not mean that many
GPUs are free right now. For current availability, request
`include=AVAILABILITY&product=POD` and read `availability`
(overall) or `dataCenters` (per data center).

pool.description: Serverless GPU pool ID (use for serverless endpoint creation). Null if GPU is not in a serverless pool.

price.description:
List price in USD per hour for a **single** GPU of this type. Pod
rates are quoted separately per cloud (`secure`, `community`);
`serverless` is the rate for this GPU's pool. In every case the
rate for a unit is the figure times `gpu.count`; the rate actually
billed for a pod is reported as `cost` on the pod itself.

serverless.description:
Serverless list price per GPU per hour, from the `pool` this GPU
belongs to. Multiply by `gpu.count` for the per-worker rate.
Absent when the GPU is not in a serverless pool available to the
caller. Negotiated account discounts are not reflected.

ListBillingResponse.description: Aggregated billing records across all Runpod resources.

ListClusterBillingResponse.description: Time-bucketed Cluster billing records plus metadata for the resolved query, record count, distinct cluster count, and compute totals.

ListEndpointBillingResponse.description: Time-bucketed Runpod public endpoint billing records plus metadata for the resolved query, record count, and total endpoint amount.

builds.description:
Build history, newest first, cursor-paginated (an omitted `limit`
defaults to 100). Page with `cursor`/`limit` to walk the full
history, or fetch any build by id via
`GET /v2/serverless/{id}/builds/{buildId}`.

endpointVersion.description: The endpoint's current configuration version. Null if unknown.

The endpoint's current configuration version. A worker whose
`version` differs is running stale config (see `worker.isStale`).
Null if unknown.

ListNetworkVolumeBillingResponse.description: Time-bucketed network volume billing records plus metadata for the resolved query, record count, distinct volume count, and storage totals.

users.description: Every member of the organization, in upstream's order.

base.description:
Base URL for worker-defined HTTP and WebSocket paths.
See [Load balancing endpoints](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/load-balancing/overview).

health.description:
Health check endpoint the load balancer will periodically ping to decide if the worker is healthy enough to receive traffic. Configurable by setting the `HEALTH_CHECK_PATH` environment variable. Defaults to `/ping` if the variable is not set.
See [Health checks](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/load-balancing/overview#health-checks) for the response codes it interprets.

LogSource.description:
Log source to include in a log stream.
- `container` — container stdout/stderr log stream
- `system`    — host lifecycle/userlogs stream

global.description:
At most one global volume, on GPU and CPU pods, with no data
center constraint. Combinable with `network` but not with
`persistent` (rejected with 400): upstream drops a persistent
disk whenever a volume is attached. Same PATCH rules as
`network`: global mounts are fixed at create, `global: []` is
rejected with 400, and `volumeId` is immutable; only `path` may
change.

Mounts.description:
Storage mounts attached to a pod. `persistent` is mutually exclusive
with both `network` and `global` (enforced at the handler with 400 if
combined). The `network` field is an array for forward compatibility
with eventual multi-network-volume support, but `maxItems` is 1 today.

PATCH semantics:
- Omitting `mounts` or sending `{}` leaves the existing mount
  unchanged.
- An explicit `network: []` is rejected with 400 (clearing mounts
  is not supported).
- Mount kind is fixed at create — a PATCH that introduces a kind
  not present at create (persistent on a network pod, network on
  a persistent pod, or any mount on a previously-mountless pod)
  is rejected with 400.
- The `volumeId` of a network mount is immutable; a PATCH that
  names a different `volumeId` is rejected with 400.
- Partial mounts are not supported — every mount entry must
  include the full schema (`size` + `path` for persistent,
  `volumeId` + `path` for network). Missing required fields → 422.

NetworkMount.description:
Reference to a NetworkVolume. Custom paths are honored at runtime on
both GPU and CPU pods. The underlying `volumeId` is immutable
post-create; the mount `path` may be changed via PATCH.

path.description: Mount path inside the container. No default — must be specified explicitly.

volumeId.description: ID of an existing NetworkVolume in the same data center as the pod.

dataCenter.description: Data center location; immutable after creation

name.description: Human-readable name (not required to be unique)

type.description: Storage tier of this volume. Set at creation and immutable.

NetworkVolumeBillingAmounts.description: Network volume storage cost, split into standard and high-performance. Backs a record's amounts and the metadata totals.

highPerformanceAmount.description: High-performance storage cost in USD for the bucket.

standardAmount.description: Standard storage cost in USD for the bucket.

totalAmount.description: Total network volume cost in USD for the bucket, across standard and high-performance storage.

recordCount.description: Number of records returned (buckets times distinct volumes).

uniqueNetworkVolumeCount.description: Number of distinct network volumes the records span.

networkVolumeId.description: The networkVolumeId filter applied, if any.
The network volume this record bills. When the networkVolumeId filter is set every record carries that id; otherwise one record is emitted per network volume per bucket.

NetworkVolumeBillingRecord.description: A single time-bucketed network volume billing record, split into standard and high-performance storage. Returned by GET /v2/billing/network-volumes.

id.description: Role ID. A built-in role's ID is `builtin:` followed by its name; a custom role carries its own ID.

OrganizationRoleType.description: Who defines the role. `builtin` roles are Runpod's: `builtin:admin`, `builtin:dev`, `builtin:billing` and `builtin:basic`. A `custom` role is one the organization defined, under its own ID.

OrganizationUser.description: A member of the caller's organization. `id` is the member's user ID.

email.description: The member's email address. Null for an account that has none.

Paginated.description: Mixin for cursor-paginated list responses. Compose it with `allOf` next to the resource's bare list schema so that a list shape shared with a non-paginated endpoint (e.g. a cluster's member pods) does not inherit a pagination block it cannot honour.

Pagination.description: Cursor-pagination metadata, uniform across list endpoints. Every response carries it: follow `nextCursor` while `hasNextPage` is true to walk the full result set.

hasNextPage.description: Whether more items exist after this page.

nextCursor.description: Pass as the `cursor` query parameter to fetch the next page. Null on the last page.

PersistentMount.description:
Host-local persistent storage. Pinned to the pod's host machine — data
does not survive a host failure. Disallowed on CPU pods. Mutually
exclusive with NetworkMount. Deprecated: prefer NetworkMount for any
data you cannot recreate.

path.description: Mount path inside the container. May be changed via PATCH.

size.description: Host-local persistent storage in GB. Upstream enforces a 10 GB floor.

actions.description: Valid state transitions for the current status.

cluster.description: Cluster membership; omitted from a standalone pod. Member pods are managed through `/v2/clusters/{id}` — they are excluded from `GET /v2/pods` by default (pass `includeClusterPods=true` to include them) and cannot be modified or deleted via the pod endpoints.

cost.description: The pod's hourly compute rate in USD. It's returned in every status, including `EXITED`, so it isn't what you're paying right now: a stopped pod isn't billed for compute, only for its volume disk.

cpu.description: Present for CPU pods; omitted from GPU pods.

cudaVersion.description: CUDA version reported by the host machine. Retained while the pod is stopped — a stopped pod keeps its machine assignment and resumes onto the same host. Null means unknown or not applicable (CPU pods, or a host that has not reported one), not that CUDA is absent.

dataCenterId.description: Data center where the pod is running (assigned by scheduler)

gpu.description: Present for GPU pods; omitted from CPU pods.

locked.description: Whether the pod is locked (prevents stopping or resetting)

runtime.description: Live utilization metrics. Null when the pod is not RUNNING, and when listing pods with `GET /v2/pods`; fetch a single pod by ID to obtain metrics.

ssh.description: SSH connection details, via the Runpod proxy or directly to the pod's published `22/tcp` port.

template.description: ID of the template this pod was created from

PodAction.description: State transition to trigger on a pod.

PodBillingAmounts.description: Pod cost components covering both GPU and CPU pods. Backs a record's amounts and the metadata totals.

cpuAmount.description: CPU pod compute cost in USD for the bucket.

diskAmount.description: Pod disk cost in USD for the bucket.

gpuAmount.description: GPU pod compute cost in USD for the bucket.

totalAmount.description: Total pod cost in USD for the bucket.

recordCount.description: Number of records returned (buckets times distinct pods).

uniquePodCount.description: Number of distinct pods the records span.

podId.description: The podId filter applied, if any.
The pod this record bills. When the podId filter is set every record carries that id; otherwise one record is emitted per pod per bucket.

PodBillingRecord.description: A single time-bucketed pod billing record, covering both GPU and CPU pods. Returned by GET /v2/billing/pods.

PodCluster.description: A pod's membership in a cluster.

id.description: ID of the cluster this pod belongs to.

ip.description: The pod's address on the cluster's private overlay network; omitted until the address is assigned.

rank.description: The pod's node rank within the cluster (NODE_RANK), or null until the index is assigned during provisioning. Rank 0 is the cluster's entry node (`Cluster.primary`); for SLURM it is the controller.

role.description: SLURM or RAY role; omitted for TRAINING/APPLICATION clusters, which do not assign roles.

PodClusterRole.description: A cluster member's role. Assigned for SLURM and RAY clusters; omitted for TRAINING/APPLICATION members.

enabled.description: Whether global networking is enabled, giving the pod a private IP reachable across data centers. Derived from whether the pod has an assigned global-network address.

internalDns.description: Internal DNS name (`<podId>.runpod.internal`), reachable from other globally-networked pods in the same account. Present only when enabled.

ip.description: The pod's assigned global-networking IP. Present only when enabled.

PodList.description: A bare list of pods. `GET /v2/clusters/{id}/pods` returns it as-is (a cluster's members are a small, complete set); `GET /v2/pods` composes it with the pagination block via ListPodsResponse.

PodRuntime.description: Live utilization metrics for a running pod.

PodRuntimePort.description: Live port mapping for a running pod.

PodSsh.description: How to connect to this pod over SSH. Both variants authenticate with the account's registered SSH public keys (`PUT /v2/account/ssh-keys`), which reach the pod only if it was created with `startSsh` — a pod created without it has no SSH access regardless of what this block reports.

direct.description: Connection straight to the pod's sshd over its published `22/tcp` mapping. Supports the full SSH feature set. Null unless `22/tcp` is in `ports` and the running pod has been assigned a public port for it — so it is usually absent while the pod is provisioning or stopped. It can still appear on a stopped pod, so check that `status` is `RUNNING` before connecting. Also null when listing pods with `GET /v2/pods`; fetch a single pod by ID to obtain the live mapping.

proxy.description: Connection through Runpod's SSH proxy. Works without exposing a port and without a public IP, but carries an interactive shell only — SCP, SFTP, rsync, and port forwarding need `direct`. Null until the pod has a machine assignment.

PodSshEndpoint.description: One way to reach the pod over SSH, as both its parts and a ready-to-run invocation.

command.description: The equivalent `ssh` invocation, ready to run. Add `-i <path>` if the matching private key is not one of your default identities, and `-o StrictHostKeyChecking=no` to skip the host-key prompt on short-lived pods.

host.description: Hostname or IP to connect to.

username.description: SSH username. For the proxy this is an opaque routing token, not a user account on the pod.

PodStatus.description:
Lifecycle status of a pod.
- `PROVISIONING` — pod is being allocated
- `STARTING`     — container is starting
- `RUNNING`      — container is healthy
- `EXITED`       — container exited (stopped)
- `ERROR`        — container is in an unrecoverable error state
- `TERMINATED`   — pod has been permanently deleted

Product.description: Catalog product availability context. Availability is product-specific, so this is required whenever availability is requested.

cancel.description:
Stop an in-progress job or remove a queued job before it starts.
See the [/cancel operation reference](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/operation-reference#/cancel) for request and response bodies.

health.description:
Overview of an endpoint's operational status.
See the [/health operation reference](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/operation-reference#/health) for request and response bodies.

purgeQueue.description:
Remove all pending jobs from the queue. Does not affect in-progress jobs.
See the [/purge-queue operation reference](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/operation-reference#/purge-queue) for request and response bodies.

retry.description:
Requeue a failed or timed-out job without submitting a new request.
See the [/retry operation reference](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/operation-reference#/retry) for request and response bodies.

run.description:
URL for asynchronously submitting a queued job.
See the [/run operation reference](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/operation-reference#/run) for request and response bodies.

runSync.description:
URL for synchronously submitting a queued job. Accepts an optional `?wait=x` query parameter to control how long the request waits for job completion, defaulting to 90 seconds.
See the [/runsync operation reference](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/operation-reference#/runsync) for request and response bodies.

status.description:
Check the current state, execution statistics, and results of a previously submitted job.
See the [/status operation reference](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/operation-reference#/status) for request and response bodies.

stream.description:
Receive incremental results as they become available from a job that generates output progressively.
See the [/stream operation reference](https://docs.runpod.io/serverless/endpoints/operation-reference#/stream) for request and response bodies.

QueueDelayScaling.description: Scale on queue wait time. Queue-based endpoints only.

queueDelay.description: Adjusts the number of workers based on how long requests wait in the queue.

type.description: Scaler discriminator. Always `QUEUE_DELAY` for this variant.

RateLimitHeader.description:
Live per-window quota state. Optional — omitted for rate-limit-exempt
callers.

A structured-field list with one member per window (`minute`, `hour`,
`day`), each carrying the remaining request count `r` and seconds until
the window resets `t`. Returned on responses to authenticated requests,
not only on 429s.

RateLimitPolicyHeader.description:
Static per-window quota policy. Optional — omitted for rate-limit-exempt
callers.

A structured-field list with one member per window (`minute`, `hour`,
`day`), each carrying the quota `q` and the window length in seconds `w`.
Returned on responses to authenticated requests, not only on 429s.

Limits are per user, and every `/v2` route counts toward the same
limits; creating pods has no separate limit. Read the current quotas from
this header instead of hard-coding them, because they can change and some
accounts have higher limits. A 429 only slows you down: wait for the
`Retry-After` time and retry. Your account isn't suspended.

buildId.description:
The GitHub build that produced this release. Set when `source` is
`GIT_BUILD`; null for `MANUAL` releases. Fetch build detail/logs via
`/v2/serverless/{id}/builds/{buildId}`.

createdByUserId.description: ID of the user who created the release.

diff.description: Configuration fields that changed in this release.

version.description: The endpoint configuration version this release produced.

workerCount.description: Workers currently running this release's version.

field.description:
The changed configuration field. Top-level (e.g. `gpuCount`,
`locations`) or template-scoped (e.g. `template.imageName`,
`template.env`).

new.description: New value, as raw JSON. Null when the field was removed.

old.description: Previous value, as raw JSON. Null when the field was added.

ReleaseSource.description:
What produced the release.
- `GIT_BUILD` — a completed GitHub build (see `buildId`)
- `MANUAL`    — a manual configuration change

RequestCountScaling.description:
Scale on concurrent in-flight requests per worker. Required for
load-balancing endpoints; also selectable for queue-based.

requestCount.description: Adjusts the number of workers based on active in-flight requests.

type.description: Scaler discriminator. Always `REQUEST_COUNT` for this variant.

inProgress.description: True while any worker is still running an older version.

percentOnLatest.description: Percentage of workers on the current version (0 when there are no workers).

workersOnLatest.description: Workers running the endpoint's current version.

workersTotal.description: All workers currently allocated to the endpoint.

Secret.description: An account-scoped secret: an encrypted string stored by Runpod, referenced from pod, serverless, and template environment variables with the `{{ RUNPOD_SECRET_<name> }}` placeholder, substituted with the secret's value when the pod or worker boots. The value is write-only and never returned by the API.

name.description: Unique, human-readable name — the `<name>` referenced by the `RUNPOD_SECRET_<name>` placeholder. Immutable after creation.

valueLastUpdatedAt.description: When the secret's value was last set (creation or rotation)

ServerlessBillingAmounts.description: Serverless cost components, inclusive of platform charges. Backs a record's amounts and the metadata totals.

cpuAmount.description: Serverless CPU compute cost in USD for the bucket.

diskAmount.description: Serverless disk cost in USD for the bucket.

feeAmount.description: Unused and always 0. Platform charges are included in the GPU and CPU amounts.

gpuAmount.description: Serverless GPU compute cost in USD for the bucket.

totalAmount.description: Total serverless cost in USD for the bucket.

recordCount.description: Number of records returned (buckets times distinct endpoints).

uniqueServerlessCount.description: Number of distinct serverless endpoints the records span.

serverlessId.description: The serverlessId filter applied, if any.
The serverless endpoint this record bills. When the serverlessId filter is set every record carries that id; otherwise one record is emitted per serverless endpoint per bucket.

ServerlessBillingRecord.description: A single time-bucketed serverless billing record. Returned by GET /v2/billing/serverless.

keys.description: The account's registered SSH public keys, one authorized_keys-style entry per element (`<type> <base64-key> [comment]`).

allowedCudaVersions.description: Acceptable CUDA versions for containers created from this template, as `major.minor`. Empty means any version. Expanded into GPU pod and serverless endpoint creates; CPU pods ignore it.

public.description: Whether this template is visible to other Runpod users

serverless.description: Whether this template is for serverless workers (true) or pods (false)

startJupyter.description: Whether containers created from this template start JupyterLab at startup (`JUPYTER_PASSWORD` env injection).

startSsh.description: Whether containers created from this template get SSH access provisioned at startup (`PUBLIC_KEY` env injection).

TemplateCategory.description:
Controls how the template is grouped and filtered in the Runpod console.
It does not affect hardware selection, scheduling, or billing.
- `CPU`    — CPU-only workloads
- `NVIDIA` — NVIDIA GPU workloads
- `AMD`    — AMD GPU workloads

TemplateList.description: A bare list of templates. `GET /v2/catalog/templates` returns it as-is (the catalog is a capped, curated set); `GET /v2/templates` composes it with the pagination block via ListTemplatesResponse.

TemplateMounts.description:
Storage mounts attached to a template. Templates support only a
single persistent mount today; any `network` property is rejected
with 422 by the schema validator.

PATCH semantics: omitting `mounts` or sending `{}` leaves the
existing mount unchanged.

UpdateClusterRequest.description:
Request body for updating a cluster. Only the cluster name can be
changed — this endpoint is a rename. Compute shape, type, and container
configuration are fixed at creation.

allowedCudaVersions.description:
Acceptable CUDA versions for worker placement, as
`major.minor`. An explicit `[]` clears the constraint;
omitting the field leaves it unchanged. Takes effect as
workers are replaced.

A non-empty set is mutually exclusive with minCudaVersion (400
if both are sent). An explicit `[]` states no constraint, so it
may accompany a floor.
Setting one does not clear the other — clear it explicitly in
the same patch if the endpoint already carries it.

minCudaVersion.description:
Lowest acceptable CUDA version for worker placement, as
`major.minor`. An explicit `""` clears the floor; omitting the
field leaves it unchanged. Takes effect as workers are
replaced.

Mutually exclusive with a non-empty allowedCudaVersions (400 if

Creates a new pod. `name` is always required; supply exactly one of
`gpu` or `cpu` to select compute (a GPU or a CPU pod). Container
settings come from the body, from a template referenced by
`templateId` (body fields override the template's), or both; `image`
is required unless `templateId` is set. See `CreatePodRequest` for
the full body.

Returns `201` with the created pod. Provisioning is asynchronous: the
pod starts in `PROVISIONING`, transitions through `STARTING`, and
reaches `RUNNING` once its container is healthy. Poll `getPod` (or
watch the pod's `status`) to observe readiness rather than assuming
the pod is running when this call returns.

## Checking what you can deploy

This endpoint places one specific GPU type. It does not search for
capacity, and it does not fall back to a different GPU. To find out
what is deployable before you call it, read the catalog:

- [List GPU types](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-gpu-types)
  — GPU types with pricing, per-cloud ceilings, and, with
  `include=AVAILABILITY&product=POD`, current pod stock.
- [List data centers](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-data-centers)
  — locations, with `include=GPU_AVAILABILITY` for stock per data
  center.

Both accept filters that combine, so you can narrow by location and by
compute in one request — for example
`GET /v2/catalog/datacenters?regions=EUROPE&include=GPU_AVAILABILITY`
returns only European data centers, each carrying the GPU types
currently available there.

## Deploying under region and GPU constraints

If you need a particular GPU in a particular geography, the working
pattern is read-then-create: narrow the catalog to an acceptable
(data center, GPU) set, then call this endpoint once per candidate in
your order of preference until one returns `201`. The runnable sample
alongside this operation does exactly that.

Availability can change between the catalog read and the create call,
so treat the catalog as a way to order your candidates, not as a
reservation — a create can still fail for capacity on a GPU the
catalog just reported as available.

Which failures are worth retrying:

| Status | Meaning | Do |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `422` | The body does not match the contract. `errors` lists each violation. | Fix the request. Never retry. |
| `400` | The body matches the contract but was rejected — either it breaks a cross-field rule, or this GPU and data center combination could not be placed. | Try your next candidate. |
| `402` | Insufficient balance. | Stop; no candidate will succeed. |
| `403` | Your account cannot access the requested pool. | Skip this candidate, keep going. |
| `429` | Rate limited. | Back off using `Retry-After`, then resume. |
| `5xx` | Transient upstream failure. | Retry the same candidate with backoff. |

Requests larger than 102400 bytes receive `413` after authentication
and rate limiting, before deployment processing. Reduce the serialized
JSON request body and retry.

This limit also applies to the deployment request built from your input
and any referenced template. A small request can therefore receive `413`
if inherited template settings make the combined request too large.
Reduce environment variables or command values in your request or template
and retry.

`400` covers both "your request breaks a rule" and "no capacity",
because capacity exhaustion currently carries no machine-readable code
of its own — only a human-readable `detail`. A rule violation is
deterministic, so it fails identically on every candidate: if *every*
candidate returns `400`, read the last `detail` as a problem with the
request rather than as absent capacity.

apply immediately while others (e.g. `globalNetworking`) take effect

post.description:
Triggers a state transition on a pod. Send a JSON body with a single
`action` field, e.g. `{ "action": "stop" }`.

Valid actions:
- `start`     — boot a stopped pod (`EXITED` or `ERROR`) back toward
  `RUNNING`.
- `stop`      — stop a running or provisioning pod, releasing GPU/CPU
  compute while keeping its disk. The pod moves to `EXITED`.
- `restart`   — restart a `RUNNING` pod's container in place.
- `terminate` — permanently delete the pod and release its resources
  (equivalent to `deletePod`).

Which actions are valid depends on the pod's current status, and the
currently permitted set is published in the pod's `actions` field:
`RUNNING` allows `stop`/`restart`/`terminate`; `EXITED` and `ERROR`
allow `start`/`terminate`; `PROVISIONING` and `STARTING` allow

post.description:
Creates a serverless endpoint. Callers specify exactly one of `gpu` or
`cpu`; neither or both returns 400. Container settings come from the
body, from a serverless template referenced by `templateId` (body
fields override the template's), or both; `image` is required unless
`templateId` is set. See `CreateEndpointRequest` for the full body.

The CUDA constraints live on `gpu` — `gpu.allowedCudaVersions` and
`gpu.minCudaVersion` — so a CPU create cannot express them and the
schema rejects the attempt with a 422. A non-empty set and a floor are
mutually exclusive (400 if both are sent); an explicit empty set states
no constraint and may accompany a floor.

Returns `201` with the created endpoint. The endpoint can accept jobs
immediately, but starts with no active workers unless `workers.min`
is greater than 0. Workers are provisioned on demand and autoscaled
between `workers.min` and `workers.max` according to the `scaling`
policy, so the first request to an idle endpoint may incur cold-start
latency while a worker pulls its image and boots.

## Checking what you can deploy

`gpu.pools` takes serverless GPU **pool** IDs, not the GPU type IDs
used for pods. `gpu.excludedTypes` takes the type IDs — it subtracts
specific cards from the pools you picked. Read both from the catalog
before you create:

- [List GPU types](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-gpu-types)
  — the `pool` field carries the pool ID for each GPU type (`null`
  means that type is not in a serverless pool). Add
  `include=AVAILABILITY&product=SERVERLESS` for current serverless
  stock.
- [List data centers](https://docs.runpod.io/api-reference-v2/catalog/list-data-centers)
  — locations to constrain with `dataCenterIds`, with
  `include=GPU_AVAILABILITY` for stock per data center.

Unlike pod creation, you do not need to retry across GPUs yourself:
list every pool you are willing to run on and workers are placed on
whichever one has capacity. Listing more pools — and leaving
`dataCenterIds` unset — gives the scheduler more room and reduces the
chance of workers failing to start when a single pool is exhausted.

If your workload needs a specific card, pick the pool that holds it and
exclude the rest of that pool with `gpu.excludedTypes`. Keep at least
one type in the selection — upstream rejects a selection that leaves
none.
